about.text: The whey left after milk is curdled with acid instead of rennet, from fresh cheeses such as cottage cheese and quark, from Greek-style yogurt, or from acid casein. It has a pH of about 4.3–5, against roughly 6 for sweet whey, and is rich in calcium phosphate and lactic acid, which make it hard to dry.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Acid whey carries more minerals than sweet whey (ash 0.7–0.8 % against 0.5 %) and is far more sour.
